# Easy Checking launch graphics: Instagram 1080 × 1080 and LinkedIn 1200 × 627 ## 1. Final copy **Headline change.** I can't use "No fees. Ever." because it isn't literally true: - Paper statements cost $2 a month. - Out-of-network ATM withdrawals cost $2.50 each. - "Ever" promises that fees will never change, and the product sheet doesn't guarantee that. The recommended headline keeps the energy and uses only absolute claims that are true. | Element | Copy (both formats) | |---|---| | **Headline (recommended)** | **$0 maintenance fee.
$0 overdraft fees.** | | Alternative A (closest to Jane's voice) | No maintenance fee. No overdraft fees. | | Alternative B (playful) | Low-maintenance checking. Literally. *(with "$0 monthly maintenance fee" as the sub-line)* | | **Rate block** | **2.25% APY\*** on balances up to $5,000 | | **Sub-line** | Built for your first account. Open with just $25. *(LinkedIn: "Built for your first account. $25 to open.")* | | **CTA** | Open online in about 5 minutes | | **Insurance** | NCUA logo + "Federally insured by NCUA" | **Disclosure (master text, identical on both formats):** > \*Rate applies to balances up to $5,000; balances above $5,000 earn 0.10% APY. APY = Annual Percentage Yield. Rates may change after account opening. $25 minimum opening deposit. Fees could reduce earnings. Paper statements $2/month (e-statements free). Out-of-network ATM withdrawals $2.50 each. Overdraft fee $0: transactions that would overdraw are declined. Valid ID required to open. Notes on the disclosure: - **Lines added beyond the excerpt.** "$25 minimum opening deposit" and "Fees could reduce earnings" are standard for rate ads under NCUA's Truth in Savings rules (Part 707). Compliance should confirm them. - **Why the other fees are listed.** Naming the paper-statement and ATM fees keeps "$0 maintenance fee" honest. - **What I left out.** The "4 network ATM fee refunds" line is ambiguous (refunds of which fees?), so it stays out until Compliance clarifies the wording. ## 2. Layout and visual direction ### Shared system - **Type:** brand sans in two weights only, Bold 700 for the headline, rate, CTA and labels, and Regular 400 for everything else. The mock-ups use Arial as a stand-in, and line lengths were checked against Arial metrics. Re-fit them once the brand font is placed. - **Colour roles and contrast:** - Sand background with Navy text (about 10:1 contrast). - Navy rate card with white numerals and Sea Glass sub-text (about 5.8:1). - Sea Glass CTA pill with Navy text. - Never use Sea Glass text on Sand, because the contrast fails. - **Hierarchy:** 1. Rate: the biggest numeral, on the highest-contrast surface. 2. Headline: the biggest text block. 3. CTA. 4. Sub-line. 5. Logo. 6. Disclosure band. - **Tone ("fun"):** rounded corners, a pill CTA, conversational copy and warm candid photography. No piggy banks, money rain or cash fans. - **Photo:** - Real members (with signed releases) at a kitchen table in morning window light. - Candid moments, such as laughing or one parent checking the app on a phone. - Faces sit in the upper part of the frame, leaving the tabletop clear where the rate card overlaps. - **Disclosure band:** always full width at the bottom, with the NCUA logo bottom-right. - Fine print is 20 px on the square and 18 px on landscape. That is legible at full size but small in the feed. - Repeat the full disclosure in the post caption and link description as well. ### Instagram 1080 × 1080 - **Grid:** 12 columns, 60 px margins, 20 px gutters, 8 px baseline. - **Photo:** full bleed across the top 440 px, with subjects in the right two-thirds. - **Rate card:** Navy, columns 1–6, straddling the bottom edge of the photo so it bridges image and copy. This puts it front and centre in the reading path. - **Copy block:** headline (76 px, above the 64 px minimum), then sub-line (30 px), then CTA pill (columns 1–6). - **Logo:** bottom-right as a sign-off, 200 px wide (minimum 160) with clear space around it. The clear space assumes a T-height of about 36 px; confirm against the master artwork. - **Footer:** a divider, then fine print in columns 1–9 and NCUA in columns 10–12 at 150 px wide (minimum 120). ### LinkedIn 1200 × 627 - **Grid:** 12 columns, 48 px margins, 24 px gutters. - **What changes:** the stack becomes side by side. - Copy column on the left (columns 1–7). - Photo on the right (columns 8–12, full height down to the footer). - **Logo:** moves top-left (180 px). On a link card, brand recognition comes first. - **Headline:** drops to 64 px so each line fits on one line. - **Rate card:** still anchored to the photo, now on its lower half. The eye runs in a Z: logo, headline, rate, CTA. - **Footer:** the disclosure band runs full width at 18 px, with NCUA at 140 px bottom-right. - **Link text:** LinkedIn shows the link title below the image, so the title should not repeat the headline. ## 3. SVG mock-ups ### Instagram feed post, 1080 × 1080 ```svg ``` ### LinkedIn link image, 1200 × 627 ```svg ``` Dashed outlines and the small grey-style labels are annotations, not final artwork. ## 4. Note to Jane Hi Jane, here's what changed from the brief and why. - **"No fees. Ever."** - Compliance only allows absolute claims that are literally true. Easy Checking charges $2/month for paper statements and $2.50 per out-of-network ATM withdrawal. - "Ever" also promises fees will never change, which we can't guarantee. - "$0 maintenance fee. $0 overdraft fees." is true and still punchy. Alternatives A and B are there if you want a different flavour. - **"Nobody else locally beats it."** - This is a comparative superiority claim with no supporting data on the product sheet, and competitor rates move. - If you want it, we'd need a dated local rate survey and Compliance sign-off. Even then, the wording would be something like "One of the highest rates in [area] as of [date]." - **2.25% APY "front and centre."** Done. It's the largest numeral on the post. It always appears with "on balances up to $5,000," because balances above that earn 0.10%. That line and the APY definition are mandatory. - **"Open in 5 minutes."** The product sheet says *about* 5 minutes with a valid ID, so the CTA says "about." The ID requirement is in the fine print. - **Overdraft.** "$0 overdraft fees" is true, but transactions are declined instead. I said so in the fine print so first-time members aren't surprised at checkout. - **Photo.** The brand guide requires real members, so we'll need a member shoot with releases rather than stock. If time allows, consider a second shot (roommates or a young couple) to reach the 22–35 first-timers who don't have kids. - **For Compliance to confirm:** - The "$25 minimum opening deposit" and "Fees could reduce earnings" lines I added for the rate disclosure. - Clearer wording for the ATM fee refunds before we mention them. Happy to walk through either format.
